steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and lightly grease a small baking dish (or have a covered non-stick pan ready for the stovetop).
Whisk the egg with the milk, sugar and a pinch of salt until well combined.
Stir in the cooked rice until every grain is coated, then tip into the prepared dish and press level.
Bake for about 20 minutes, or cook covered over low heat on the stovetop, until the egg has set and the top is lightly golden.
Let it cool for a few minutes, then swirl or spoon the strawberry jam over the top.
Cut into 4 pieces and serve warm or at room temperature.
Rinse the quinoa under cold water, then add to a small saucepan with the water or oat milk.
Bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the quinoa is tender and the liquid is mostly absorbed.
Stir in a pinch of cinnamon and remove from the heat.
Slice the banana and spoon the porridge into a bowl.
Top with the banana slices and mixed berries, then drizzle with the maple syrup.
In a bowl, stir together the cooked rice, milk, honey and a pinch of cinnamon until well combined.
Divide the mixture between airtight containers or jars to make 3 servings.
Cover and refrigerate overnight so the rice absorbs the milk and softens.
In the morning, stir each portion loose, adding a splash more milk if it's too thick.
Top with the mixed berries and an extra pinch of cinnamon before serving.
Set up a steamer or idli cooker with water and bring it to the boil.
Steam the idlis for 5-10 minutes, until soft and hot through.
Meanwhile, warm the sambar in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until simmering.
Spoon the sambar into a bowl and add the coconut chutney to one side.
Plate the idlis alongside and serve immediately while hot.
Rinse the poha briefly in a sieve under cold water and set aside to soften for a few minutes.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the peanuts until golden, then remove and set aside.
Add the mustard seeds and curry leaves to the same pan; once the seeds pop, add the chopped onion and peas and cook for 3-4 minutes until the onion softens.
Stir in the turmeric, then add the softened poha and toss well to coat and heat through, about 2 minutes.
Stir the fried peanuts back in, squeeze over the lime juice, and serve hot.
Dry-roast the semolina in a pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly, until lightly golden and fragrant, then tip out and set aside.
In the same pan, heat the oil and add the mustard seeds; once they pop, add the curry leaves, chopped green chilli and onion, and cook for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add the diced carrot and peas and cook for another 2 minutes.
Pour in the water and bring to the boil.
Reduce the heat, slowly stir in the roasted semolina to avoid lumps, then cover and cook for 2-3 minutes until the water is absorbed and the upma is fluffy.
In a bowl or jar, combine the rolled oats, apple juice or milk, yogurt, grated apple, sultanas and a pinch of cinnamon.
Stir well until everything is evenly mixed.
Cover and refrigerate overnight so the oats soften and soak up the liquid.
In the morning, stir through the honey, adding a splash more milk or juice if it's too thick.
Serve chilled.
In a large bowl or jug, whisk together the milk, Greek yogurt, protein powder and honey until smooth.
Stir in the rolled oats until fully combined.
Divide the mixture evenly between 5 jars or containers.
Cover and refrigerate overnight until thickened.
Top each jar with berries just before serving.
Whisk the GF pancake mix (or rice flour and oat flour) with the eggs and milk until you have a smooth, lump-free batter.
Slice the banana and fold half of it into the batter, saving the rest for topping.
Melt a little of the butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat and ladle in small portions of batter.
Cook for 1-2 minutes per side, until bubbles appear on the surface and the edges set, then flip and cook until golden.
Repeat with the remaining batter and butter to make about 8 pancakes.
Stack the pancakes, top with the remaining banana slices and drizzle with the maple syrup.
Whisk the buckwheat flour and baking powder together in a bowl.
Add the eggs and rice milk and whisk until you have a smooth batter.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick pan over medium heat and pour in a portion of the batter.
Cook for 1-2 minutes until bubbles form and the edges look set, then flip and cook for another minute until golden.
Repeat with the remaining batter, stacking the pancakes as you go.
Top with the mixed berries and drizzle with the honey to serve.
Blend the rolled oats to a fine flour if not already done, then tip into a bowl with the baking powder, cinnamon and plant protein, if using.
Mash the bananas well and whisk them into the dry ingredients along with the oat milk until you have a thick, smooth batter.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick pan over medium-low heat and spoon in portions of the batter.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the edges look dry and small bubbles form, then flip carefully and cook for another 2 minutes until cooked through.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve warm.
Whisk the flour and baking powder together, then whisk in the eggs and buttermilk until you have a smooth batter.
Preheat the waffle iron and lightly grease it, then pour in enough batter to cover the plates.
Cook for 3-4 minutes until golden and crisp, then repeat with the remaining batter to make about 6 waffles.
Cool the waffles completely, then freeze any you're not eating immediately in a sealed bag or container.
To serve, toast or reheat waffles from frozen until hot and crisp, then top with the Greek yogurt, mixed berries and a drizzle of maple syrup.
Whisk the eggs, rice milk and a pinch of cinnamon together in a shallow dish.
Dip each slice of GF bread into the mixture, turning to coat both sides and letting it soak for a few seconds.
Heat a little oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and fry the soaked bread for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Cut the slices in half if needed to serve 2, then top with the berries and drizzle with the maple syrup.
Roughly chop the kale or spinach and the beetroot.
Add the greens, beetroot, bananas and mixed berries to a blender.
Pour in the coconut water, then add the chia, hemp seeds and flax.
Blend on high for 30-60 seconds until completely smooth, adding a splash more coconut water if it's too thick.
Pour into a glass and drink immediately.
